issues.description: The solution implementation declares lecture attributes using snake_case names (e.g. number_of_inscribed_students) but the constructor and all getters/setters/methods refer to camelCase names (e.g. numberOfInscribedStudents). This inner-artifact naming inconsistency in the solution causes compilation errors and contradicts the UML and problem description which use camelCase attribute names, preventing students from using the solution as a correct reference.
issues.suggestedFix: Make attribute identifiers consistent with the UML and the rest of the code. Rename the declared fields in the solution to camelCase (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors) OR consistently change all uses to match the declared snake_case names. Prefer aligning the field names to the UML/camelCase to match the problem statement and template expectations.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify camelCase attribute names (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors), but the solution implementation declares fields using snake_case (lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, number_of_guest_students, number_of_lecturers, number_of_tutors) while other parts of the same solution (constructor, getters/setters, toString) reference camelCase names. This mismatch creates confusion and breakage: students expecting the attributes from the UML will find inconsistent identifiers in the reference solution and may be unable to map requirements to the implementation or compile the code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make identifier names consistent: rename the fields in the solution to use the camelCase names from the UML (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors) and update all references (constructor assignments, getters, setters, toString, addGuestStudents) to use those same names; alternatively, if snake_case is preferred, update the constructor and all method references to consistently use the snake_case field names throughout the solution and reflect that choice in the UML/problem text.
